page: Amazon Web Services i4i.metal is a bare-metal, storage-optimized server powered by Intel Xeon 8375C processors. It features 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores with a base frequency of 3.5 GHz and a dedicated CPU allocation. The system is equipped with 1024.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage consists of 30,000 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, and the network interface delivers a baseline bandwidth of 75 Gbps. No graphics processing units are included.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core performance, with the server achieving top-tier results in Passmark CPU tests, extended instructions, and encryption processing. Multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench tests place the instance in the top 25% of evaluated hardware. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks show strong read and write capabilities. Single-core performance, including single-threaded gzip compression and Geekbench single-core scores, falls within the average range.

Given its massive local NVMe SSD storage capacity and high memory allocation, the i4i.metal is designed for data-intensive workloads. It is highly suitable for large-scale databases, high-throughput Redis deployments, and intensive database operations, as supported by strong Passmark database and Redis SET benchmark results. The bare-metal architecture eliminates hypervisor overhead, offering high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for enterprise-grade storage and transactional processing workloads.
